item.title: World Bank and UYEP to visit urban youths in Alotau
item.description: A high-level delegation from the World Bank and Urban Youth Employment Project two (UYEP II) will visit Alotau, Milne Bay Province, from tomorrow (20.09.26), to explore skills development, employment, and economic opportunities for youths in the Alotau District. ‎The four-day visit is themed "From Skills to Employment: Connecting Alotau youths with Infrastructure, skills development and Local Econ
item.content:encoded:
A high-level delegation from the World Bank and Urban Youth Employment Project two (UYEP II) will visit Alotau, Milne Bay Province, from tomorrow (20.09.26), to explore skills development, employment, and economic opportunities for youths in the Alotau District.

‎The four-day visit is themed "From Skills to Employment: Connecting Alotau youths with Infrastructure, skills development and Local Economic Opportunities",

‎The high-level consultation will bring together the World Bank, UYEP II, Alotau District and its stakeholders to assess the district's priorities, implementation readiness and opportunities for the proposed Urban Youth Employment Program under phase three (III).

‎The mission will include practical field visits to potential urban work sites, technical and vocational schools, training institutions and local employers.

‎The World Bank team will be led by Elaine Chee, assisted by four other officers, while the team from the UYEP II will be led by the Project Coordination Manager, Tom Gilis, accompanied by one other officer.

The consultation is expected to provide more employment opportunities for youths while strengthening the connection between urban infrastructure improvement, vocational training, local employment and private-sector participation.

‎The Urban Youth Employment Project is a World Bank- backed initiative in PNG designed to help disadvantaged and unemployed young people.

item.title: Sixty bike riders from Kainantu arrive in Goroka for the 70th show
item.description: Sixty bike riders from Obura-Wonenara and Kainantu districts of Eastern Highlands Province ride their bicycle on Thursday night and turn up in the Provincial capital on Friday morning. They decorate their bikes with PNG flag and the provincial flag as it is part of the Independence celebrations and also for the 70th Goroka Show.
item.content:encoded:
Sixty bike riders from Obura-Wonenara and Kainantu districts of Eastern Highlands Province ride their bicycle on Thursday night and turn up in the Provincial capital on Friday morning.

They decorate their bikes with PNG flag and the provincial flag as it is part of the Independence celebrations and also for the 70th Goroka Show.

They left Kainantul town at 6pm in the afternoon and ride all the way to Goroka.

Spokesperson Joshua Simon from Obura Wonenara said the main idea is to come and take part and be part of the Goroka show.

Simon said this is the 4th time for them to ride on bicycle from Kainantu to Goroka.

He said Goroka show committee did not let them into the show arena in the past years but they are hopeful this will not happen this year.

He said we are not disappointed, we are proud Eastern Highlanders and this is our time, it happens once a year and we are happy to be part of the show.

Eastern Highlands Governor Simon Sia is aware of their coming and said will organise their entry into the Show ground.

item.title: Boxers learn from Kokoda’s history
item.description: Eleven Papua New Guinea boxers got to appreciate the lessons from war heroes in World War two when they participated in a camping program on the Kokoda track on 5th September, 2026. The athletes were accompanied by staff members from the Papua New Guinea Olympic Committee and PNG Boxing National Coach, Peter Morrison.
item.content:encoded:
Eleven Papua New Guinea boxers got to appreciate the lessons from war heroes in World War two when they participated in a camping program on the Kokoda track on 5th September, 2026.

The athletes were accompanied by staff members from the Papua New Guinea Olympic Committee and PNG Boxing National Coach, Peter Morrison.

The program was sponsored by Adventure Kokoda and was also a good bonding event for the athletes who had returned from the recent Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Scotland.

Morrison who organised the trip, said the aim of the camp was to foster a sense of teamwork and national pride by learning about the sacrifices and service of the Fuzzy Wuzzy Angels and the servicemen of Papua who served alongside the Australians.

The team also participated in a teamwork challenge by making and carrying a stretcher over the homeward stretch of the trail and undertook a group discussion on the importance of role models and how each athlete saw themselves as a role model.

PNG Olympic Committee staff member and athlete performance expert, John Tekwie Jr. said it was a very humbling experience.

“It was humbling to have had such an opportunity to walk, and see first hand the physical challenges of the environment that our forefathers had gone through to allow us the freedom we enjoy now,” he said.

“In my line of work, where i represent the country, it was good to understand the importance of struggles and challenges involved in the journey towards achieving something memorable, in sports and outside.”

The team also visited the Bomana War Cemetery and paid their respects as part of the programme.

Though the programme was brief, much was learned and appreciated from the courage, mateship, service, sacrifice and commitment of the brave soldiers on Kokoda.

In their own way, athletes like these boxers also make sacrifices and commitment for their individual and collective goals in their sport and life. Morrison hopes that from this experience the team can build themselves not only as athletes but as leaders carrying a legacy that was hard fought for on those treacherous tracks over 80 years ago.

The boxers will be resuming full training soon in preparation for the Pacific Games in Tahiti in 2027. Those who make the final team will carry the hopes of their country and their people, and hopefully, in their hearts and minds, they also carry the memories and stories of those who went before them.

item.title: 50 illegal firearms surrendered in Tari
item.description: About 50 high-powered illegal firearms were publicly displayed in Tari town following a voluntary surrender by local community members under Papua New Guinea’s national gun amnesty initiative. Among the weapons showcased were several that had been safely safeguarded by John Tipa (Hela Provincial Election Manager) from a previous surrender campaign.
item.content:encoded:
About 50 high-powered illegal firearms were publicly displayed in Tari town following a voluntary surrender by local community members under Papua New Guinea’s national gun amnesty initiative.

Among the weapons showcased were several that had been safely safeguarded by John Tipa (Hela Provincial Election Manager) from a previous surrender campaign.

​The event was attended by Minister for Police Sir John Pundari, Hela Governor Philip Undialu, Koroba Lake Kopiago MP William Bando, Tari Residential Judge Justice Andrew Kostopoulos, Acting Commissioner of Police Dr. Philip Mitna, Hela Provincial Police Commander Arau Mairi, senior police headquarters officers and community leaders.

Six brand-new police vehicles were officially handed over to the Hela Police Command to boost mobility and operational response times.

Police Minister, Sir John announced a final extension of the grace period, issuing a stern deadline for all remaining illegal firearm holders to surrender their weapons by December 15.

"From police and PNGDF Intel, we know who owns illegal guns in Enga, Hela, and Southern Highlands Provinces. We will come straight to your house," Sir John Pundari warned. "You have an opportunity now—a golden opportunity—to surrender them before it's too late."

​Substantial cash rewards are being provided to individuals who voluntarily hand over high-powered weapons. Minister Sir John said, if an individual refuses to surrender and is subsequently reported, the monetary reward will be paid to the informant, while the offender faces life in prison. ​ He announced that advanced drone technology capable of locating concealed illegal firearms will soon be deployed across Hela Province to hunt down un-surrendered weapons.

Police Minister commended and acknowledged the men who stepped forward to surrender the initial 50 high-powered weapons. He urged remaining firearm holders to follow their example before time runs out.

item.title: New facility to improve soldier welfare
item.description: PNG Defence Force engineers in Lae now have improved accommodation after more than K1 million was spent renovating their barracks at Igam. The 48-bedroom Bravo Company facility was officially handed over on Friday. The project was funded through Australia’s Defence Cooperation Program and completed by local contractor Hornibrooks.
item.content:encoded:
PNG Defence Force engineers in Lae now have improved accommodation after more than K1 million was spent renovating their barracks at Igam.

The 48-bedroom Bravo Company facility was officially handed over on Friday. The project was funded through Australia’s Defence Cooperation Program and completed by local contractor Hornibrooks.

The renovation is aimed at giving soldiers a safer place to live and rest while carrying out their duties.

Engineering Battalion commander Lieutenant Colonel Sarufa Eka said the project was about more than a building.

“It’s for our soldiers’ welfare and it helps or keeps our soldiers motivated,” Eka said.

He said soldiers needed proper accommodation so they could rest and do their jobs. The need for the work was raised by Australian Defence Force personnel in Lae.

Major Darren Cocker, the ADF officer commanding Lae, said more than K1 million was secured from Australian defence funding to refurbish the building.

"The work has made the accommodation safer and fit for purpose," he said.

The Australian Consul-General Brenton Kanowski said good accommodation was important to the welfare and morale of soldiers.

“We cannot contribute to the defence of our countries without having well-trained and fit and safely housed and looked after soldiers and personnel,” he said.

The project is part of wider defence cooperation between PNG and Australia under the Defence Cooperation Program and the Pukpuk Treaty.

It follows the recent handover of a renovated barracks to the Joint Forces Academy at Igam Barracks.

For Bravo Company soldiers, the project delivers a basic need: a safer place to live, rest and prepare for duty.

item.title: Take responsibility and shape your future, says Morris

item.content:encoded: ‎'Being independent means taking control of our destiny'; that was the message delivered to the people of Alotau, Milne Bay, during the 51st Independence celebrations on Wednesday. ‎ ‎Indigenous people of the province have been challenged to rise and take ownership of their land and resources, create local businesses and contribute in building the nation's economy, as foreign businesses continue to expand in the province. ‎ ‎For 51 years, Papua New Guinea has lived as an independent nation but as the country looks towards the future, questions remain about how much control the nation has over its own economic development, despite the abundant natural resources, land and tourism potential. ‎ ‎Speaking during the Independence celebrations in Alotau, local MP Ricky Morris challenged the people to take greater ownership of their resources, build and own local businesses and work collectively to contribute to the nation's development. ‎ ‎“Milne Bay is rich with blessings. We have fertile land suitable for growing cash crops, we have seas full of fish with islands that attract tourism and cultures admired throughout the world," he said. ‎ ‎"This is how we will lift our socio and economic strength of our electorate, province and our country. A future that is free from foreign influence, respect for each other and the laws of our land. ‎ ‎"Our freedom, our rights, and our vision guided by our unique constitution that many of us fall short to understand." ‎ ‎With foreign businesses continuing to expand in the province, Morris also appealed to the Milne Bay Provincial Government [MBPG] to make it easier for indigenous landowners to access and develop their land for business purposes. ‎ ‎He said creating simpler processes would allow more local people to establish businesses, participate in Small and Medium Enterprises, and benefit directly from economic opportunities created within the province. ‎ ‎Morris also called on the provincial government to consider legislation aimed at protecting and strengthening indigenous businesses as they compete with foreign-owned enterprises. ‎ ‎

item.title: Public servants told to return to work
item.description: Hela Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu says this 51st Independence Anniversary must mark a turning point - a time when all public servants in Hela unite and commit to serving the people. Speaking during the Independence celebrations in Tari, Angu issued a stern warning to absentee public servants who continue to draw salaries while living outside the province.
item.content:encoded:
Hela Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu says this 51st Independence Anniversary must mark a turning point - a time when all public servants in Hela unite and commit to serving the people.

Speaking during the Independence celebrations in Tari, Angu issued a stern warning to absentee public servants who continue to draw salaries while living outside the province.

"After these celebrations, going forward, all provincial and district public servants must be seen at their respective workplaces," he declared.

"I do not want public servants who are living outside the province and collecting pay. It is time to change and they must return to their workplaces in Hela Province," he said.

Mr. Angu reiterated that any public servant who remains outside the province while still collecting a government salary will be terminated.

Mr. Angu, who is also Chairman of the Hela Provincial Liquor Licensing Board, said his biggest challenge is public servants themselves defying the province-wide liquor ban.

He revealed that he has now directed a section of the PNG Defence Force to conduct road checks on all vehicles - including public servants, police and PNGDF vehicles - not just civilians.

"As I speak today, 75 cartons of beer have been confiscated and some public servants have been arrested and are now locked up at the Tari Police Cell Block. Our message has been very clear on the liquor ban. Public servants have a duty to educate their communities on the liquor ban, not to be seen drinking around," he said.

He said the enforcement will continue and no one will be exempt from the ban. Ends//.

item.title: Madang scales down on sectoral programs amidst ongoing El Nino climate
item.description: The Madang Provincial Government has scaled down funding support to the various sectors in the provincial administration amidst the ongoing El Nino climate. Governor Ramsey Pariwa announced the scaling down during the 51st Independence Anniversary celebrations on Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
The Madang Provincial Government has scaled down funding support to the various sectors in the provincial administration amidst the ongoing El Nino climate.

Governor Ramsey Pariwa announced the scaling down during the 51st Independence Anniversary celebrations on Wednesday.

He has also sent out a public notice dated September 10, explaining the same.

Pariwa said as a responsible government, they have scaled down on some sectoral activities and programs, including sports and Independence events. He said they're focusing attention and funding support towards the provincial El Nino relief efforts in the wards and local level governments.

Funding assistance and any other support towards communities affected by the ongoing El Nino will be based on the respective assessment reports from the wards and LLGs, starting from this time until the El Nino impacts subside.

"DDAs have also made similar decisions as the provincial government. As your governor, I want to apologise to everyone, especially school boards, council wards, and LLGs, that we are not able to give you support to have your own Independence celebrations," Pariwa said.

He added that as a responsible government, MPG has taken appropriate measures to scale down on funding support on projects and activities in all sectors.

"Your understanding of the El Nino situation faced in the province is appreciated, and we expect your cooperation and adherence throughout this time," Pariwa said.

The governor is also urging all LLGs that have not yet furnished reports on the situations in their respective areas to do so immediately so that they can be eligible to receive some forms of assistance from the National Government.

Sumkar's LLGs, Sumgilbar, North, and South Karkar were the first to complete their assessment reports and have used them to compile the Sumkar District report, which has been presented to Governor Pariwa.

Bogia and Usino-Bundi districts are understood to be working on theirs as well.
